sourceBindings.text: Correct the three-year arrow cycle
Three cards read Year 1 maize, Year 2 soybean and Year 3 wheat, but arrows point Year 1→3→2→1.
Read the printed year numbers and crop order first.
Draw Year 1 maize → Year 2 soybean → Year 3 wheat → Year 1 maize.
Under each arrow, add the conditional nutrient, pest-host, root, residue or season purpose.
1 maize → 2 soybean → 3 wheat → 1 maize; the arrows must match the written sequence.

sourceBindings.text: Justify the adviser case model
The supplied 10-ha temperate case has low tested N after three maize years. A model proposes soybean → maize → potato.
Year 1 soybean is considered for rotation diversity and possible N fixation after checking nodulation and fit.
Year 2 maize uses the field under a crop-specific N plan, not a presumed complete N refund.
Year 3 potato changes crop family and cultivation needs; examine pest history, water, equipment and market before calling it a fit.
This is one conditional, three-year teaching model. The correct answer is the reasoned sequence, not the mere names.

sourceBindings.text: A different valid answer needs different evidence
A student suggests a suitable legume → maize → wheat, plus a fourth-year clover cover crop.
Check whether wheat and clover fit the model season and water supply, and whether the clover occupies a full year or an interval.
Compare N and residue claims with actual harvest and management; do not award a fixed fertiliser credit.
Check equipment, market, pest hosts and what happens before the cycle restarts.
Accept if each year and transition is supported by site and management evidence, with clear cover-crop timing. Other evidence-based plans are also possible.

sourceBindings.text: A pest example is conditional
Someone says soybean after maize kills every corn rootworm and is therefore mandatory on every farm.
Rotation to a non-host can reduce some host-specific pests where they actually occur.
Rootworm species and populations differ; extended diapause or rotation-adapted behaviour can weaken a simple one-year pattern.
An Egyptian field needs local identification and scouting rather than an imported pest diagnosis.
Use the example to explain a mechanism, not a guarantee or local pest claim.
